source: Center points are real OpenStreetMap coordinates found via Nominatim, all located within Princeton's real administrative boundary: Witherspoon-Jackson and Western Section are actual place=neighbourhood nodes in OSM; Princeton University's center is the amenity=university relation's centroid (used to represent the 'University' campus neighborhood); Palmer Square's center is OSM's landuse=retail feature for the square itself. None of Princeton's informal neighborhoods have official boundary polygons anywhere in OSM, so the regions shown on the map are computed (nearest-point / Voronoi) from these real centers and clipped to Princeton's real city boundary — they are a reasonable approximation, not surveyed lines.
